Title: Chocolate
Comment:
So pictures this: it’s an early morning in 2012 during my senior year of high school. I pick my best friend, B, up from her house to go to school. She hooks her iPod up to my cassette player AUX in my 1995 Lexus LE and she plays this. I’m floored. They’re British, the guitar slaps, I can’t really understand what they’re saying but I’m IN TO IT. From this point forward we blast ‘Chocolate’ by The 1975 on the way to school every morning while I’m running red lights and hitting curbs trying to get to school on time. It reminds me of how simple life used to be and how much my taste in music transformed after this.

(Quick disclaimer: I reaaaally dislike Matty Healy now).

Title: Wish You Were Here
Comment:
I grew up listening to Pink Floyd. I’d lay on my parents’ bed with my dad, listening to their music, feeling like they were in the room with us. The Wall was my first ever concert, and it set a high bar for the level of performance I expect at shows. When my dad had a heart attack and was in a coma, I played this song for him, and when he was unresponsive to everything he heard this music and his heart rate picked up (he later woke up and has been the picture of health ever since).

I listened to this song my first week in my dorm, my first time away from home. I listened to it when I was in another country by myself for the first time. I listened to it when each of my childhood pets died.

I don’t know if it’s my favorite song of all time, but it gives me comfort when I’m alone or sad and want to immerse myself in music.

Title: Note To Self
Comment: MoBo is my favorite band so any song could have been picked, but I think I listen to this one the most. This band is why I have my job and pursued music, they brought me to Philly where I met some of the most important people to me and had the best experiences. I will always think of that time of my life when listening to them. Lyrically, the band is poetic, full of quips, and raw, narrowing in on the time of being 18-25 through a cycle of 3 albums before going on a permanent hiatus. The influence they had on the diy scene single handedly shaped the emo/post-hardcore revival of 2012-16. I could go on forever but anyway MoBo 4ever<3
